newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Timan Pechora gives Russian Rosneft oil deal stake.
newsitem.headline: Timan Pechora gives Russian Rosneft oil deal stake.

text.p: The Timan Pechora Co LLC, or TPC, international oil consortium said on Tuesday it had awarded Russian state oil holding firm Rosneft a 20 percent stake in its $20 billion production-sharing deal in the Russian Arctic.

"Rosneft's 20 percent stake is all finalised and is a formality," TPC President and Chief Executive Officer Frank Ingriselli told an energy conference. The Western partners in TPC are Exxon Corp, Amoco Corp, affiliates of Texaco Inc and Norsk Hydro.
He said a final signing for the stake transfer would take place in about two weeks.
Rosneft receives its share from current shareholders. Texaco and Exxon, each of which had a 30 percent stake, each gave Rosneft six percent.
Amoco and Norsk Hydro, each of which had 20 percent, each gave Rosneft four percent.
Rosneft is the Russian government's agent in all production sharing deals.

TPC was set up in 1994 to explore, appraise and develop oil fields within a contract area in the Russian Arctic's Timan Pechora basin, in the Nenetsk autonomous region. TPC has estimated total capital expenditure over the life of the contract at $20 billion.
The contract area has potential recoverable crude oil reserves of 306 million tonnes (2.2 billion barrels). The group is still awaiting final government approval for its project.
